title: Everyone’s building a ‘GPT for cells.’ Relation’s bet is manufacturing the data to train it.

content_html:
The race to build an AI “foundation model of the cell” has a fuel problem. The biological data needed to train one is scarce, messy and inconsistent. Relation Therapeutics thinks the answer is to manufacture that data itself, and GSK is paying up to $110m to help.

The London startup unveiled two things at once on Thursday. The first is MORGAN, its flagship cellular foundation model. The second is an expanded collaboration with GSK to generate the data that feeds it.

A model of how cells respond

MORGAN, short for Multi-Omic Regulatory Genomics using Artificial Neural Networks, is meant to predict how a human cell reacts to a genetic tweak or a drug. Get that right, and you can spot disease mechanisms and new drug targets on a computer, before touching a lab bench. It is the same idea behind a foundation model of the chest or the AI-biology work at DeepMind’s Isomorphic.

Relation’s pitch is not the model alone. It is the data behind it. Models like this are only as good as what they learn from, and human biology data is thin. So Relation is building automated labs that run cellular experiments at what it calls “superhuman consistency.” They generate “petascale” datasets of how cells respond to interventions over time.

Why GSK is paying

That data factory is what GSK is buying into. Under the deal, Relation can receive up to $110m in upfront and milestone payments. In return it will generate large-scale human “perturbation” data and deploy it into models including MORGAN. The datasets capture how cells respond to genetic and pharmacological changes, which GSK wants for finding new drug targets.

“The future of drug discovery depends on our ability to understand how human cells respond to disease and treatment at an unprecedented level of detail,” said Relation’s chief executive David Roblin. He calls MORGAN and the lab behind it “the scientific infrastructure” for the next wave of drug discovery.

A crowded, unproven field

Relation is not alone in betting biology can be modelled. Well-funded rivals from Chai Discovery to a growing field of AI-bio labs are chasing versions of the same prize. Pharma is signing AI research pacts at a fast clip.

The claims are big. Relation told Endpoints News its approach could deliver “transformationally different success rates” in drug discovery. That remains to be proven. Most drugs still fail in trials, and no cell foundation model has yet produced an approved medicine. What the GSK deal shows is that Big Pharma is now willing to pay for the data, not just the drug.

content_html_zh:
构建人工智能“细胞基础模型”的竞赛存在燃料问题。 训练所需的生物数据稀缺、混乱且不一致。 Relation Therapeutics 认为答案是自己制造这些数据，葛兰素史克 (GSK) 正在支付高达 1.1 亿美元的费用来提供帮助。

这家伦敦初创公司周四同时公布了两件事。 第一个是 MORGAN，其旗舰蜂窝基础型号。 第二个是扩大与葛兰素史克的合作，以生成为其提供数据的数据。

细胞如何反应的模型

MORGAN 是使用人工神经网络的多组学调控基因组学的缩写，旨在预测人类细胞对基因调整或药物的反应。 如果做到了这一点，您就可以在接触实验室工作台之前在计算机上发现疾病机制和新的药物靶标。 这与 DeepMind 的 Isomorphic 的胸部基础模型或人工智能生物学工作背后的想法相同。

Relation 的定位不仅仅在于模型。 这是其背后的数据。 像这样的模型的好坏取决于它们从中学到的东西，而人类生物学数据却很薄弱。 因此，Relation 正在建立自动化实验室，以所谓的“超人一致性”进行细胞实验。 他们生成“千万级”数据集，展示细胞如何随时间响应干预措施。

葛兰素史克为何付费

葛兰素史克正在收购这个数据工厂。 根据协议，Relation 可以获得高达 1.1 亿美元的预付款和里程碑付款。 作为回报，它将生成大规模的人类“扰动”数据，并将其部署到包括 MORGAN 在内的模型中。 这些数据集捕获了细胞如何响应遗传和药理变化，葛兰素史克希望利用这些数据来寻找新的药物靶点。

Relation 首席执行官 David Roblin 表示：“药物发现的未来取决于我们以前所未有的详细程度了解人类细胞如何响应疾病和治疗的能力。” 他称 MORGAN 及其背后的实验室为下一波药物发现的“科学基础设施”。

一个拥挤的、未经证实的领域

关系并不是唯一可以对生物学进行建模的赌注。 从 Chai Discovery 到不断发展的人工智能生物实验室，资金雄厚的竞争对手都在追逐同一奖项的版本。 制药公司正在快速签署人工智能研究协议。

索赔金额很大。 Relation 告诉 Endpoints News，其方法可以在药物发现方面带来“彻底不同的成功率”。 这还有待证明。 大多数药物在试验中仍然失败，并且还没有细胞基础模型生产出批准的药物。 葛兰素史克的交易表明，大型制药公司现在愿意为数据付费，而不仅仅是药物。
